newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-GOLF-Somervaille ready in Eisenhower Champs.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-GOLF-Somervaille ready in Eisenhower Champs.

text.p: David Somervaille intends showing a little more aggression on Friday after leading New Zealand's scoring on the first day of the Eisenhower Cup amateur golf championship here on Thursday, NZPA reports from Manila.
Despite playing a little conservatively, the 24-year-old Aucklander fired an impressive two-under-par 70 on The Legends course during a calm, fine morning to card the day's 15th lowest score.

Richard Hislop shot a fine one-under 71 on the tougher Masters layout to be the next-best Kiwi, while Richard Best (Legends) rattled home with three late birdies for a 74 and an ailing Simon Bittle (Masters) carded a 75.

Bittle is the team's unofficial non-counting scorer at this point, which leaves them in 11th place at one-under, 11 behind the in-form Australians, who lead Finland by four and Sweden and the Philippines by six.

Australia's Brett Partridge fired a superb seven-under 65 but he was still overshadowed by Sweden's Daniel Olsson, who plundered The Legends in eight-under 64 for an Eisenhower Cup first-round record.
After carding six straight birdies from the 10th to 15th holes, he also set a nine-hole cup record of seven-under 29.

Despite being off the pace, the New Zealanders feel primed to improve their position substantially tomorrow with Somervaille expressing satisfaction mixed with slight regret that he didn't press a little bit harder in light of some of the low scores returned on The Legends.
"All in all I'm pleased but tomorrow I could probably get a little more aggressive," he said.
"I'm having trouble clubbing myself into greens which makes you a little cautious, and it was a day of near-misses for me with my putter.
"From 30 feet you're not going to make many but they all add up and I had three in a row that just missed the edge and if they drop, then I'll have a very good day."

Somervaille made birdies at the fifth, 10th and 11th before a solitary bogey at the 17th, and said the key to his round had been keeping the ball in the middle of the fairway, which opened up most of the greens.
"You just have to be a little cautious and that's probably what I was, with it being my first Eisenhower," he said.
"I also played a little tentatively because I haven't been hitting the ball that well over here. In fact I've been struggling, so all-in-all I was pleased."
Coach Mal Tongue was also upbeat about his side's situation at the end of day one.
"I think we've had a good day and I feel we've done a lot better than our 11th placing. We're not that far off of the leaders," he said.
"Dave's been building up all week and he played really solid, and I was extremely pleased for Richard (Hislop) because he was playing the harder course and I knew 71 or 72 would be a good score.
"Richard (Best) has been crook, and he's still a bit off-colour with his game, and I thought Simon was brilliant. He didn't know where he was the last five or six holes but he hung in there."
Tongue said Best's finish of three consecutive birdies had not only rescued a bad score, it had given the Blenheim youngster a wonderful lift.

"That was brilliant from a mental point of view. He played reasonably well for the first 10 holes but then lost it until he sunk a bit of a lucky putt at 16 and then had two good birdies to finish. It will give him a bit of encouragement and he'll only get better."
Hislop was satisfied with his round especially as he felt he had not hit the ball particularly well.
"I wouldn't want to go out and try and shoot that (71) again, because I didn't play that great," he said after mixing birdies at the 15th, 3rd, 4th and 6th with bogeys at the 12th, 2nd and 8th.
"I didn't play as confidently as I probably should have, but that's what you should expect in your first Eisenhower.
"But I putted really well today and thought my way around the course."
Leading first round scores, with lowest score not counted (* denoted likely non-counting NZ score):
210 - The Philippines (68, 68, 74), Sweden (64, 73, 73)
211 - United States (69, 71, 71)
212 - South Korea (69, 70, 73)
213 - Canada (70, 71, 72), Spain (69, 71, 73), Great Britain-Ireland (69, 71, 73), India (70, 71, 72)
215 - NEW ZEALAND (DAVID SOMERVAILLE 70, RICHARD HISLOP 71, RICHARD BEST 74, SIMON BITTLE 75), Italy (70, 71, 74), The Netherlands (71, 72, 72), Portugal (69, 70, 76).
